Instructions from: [redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-doctor/node_modules/bun-types/CLAUDE.md
Default to using Bun instead of Node.js.

- Use `bun <file>` instead of `node <file>` or `ts-node <file>`
- Use `bun test` instead of `jest` or `vitest`
- Use `bun check` instead of `tsc --noEmit`
- Use `bun build <file.html|file.ts|file.css>` instead of `webpack` or `esbuild`
- Use `bun install` instead of `npm install` or `yarn install` or `pnpm install`
- Use `bun run <script>` instead of `npm run <script>` or `yarn run <script>` or `pnpm run <script>`
- Use `bunx <package> <command>` instead of `npx <package> <command>`
- Bun automatically loads .env, so don't use dotenv.

## APIs

- `Bun.serve()` supports WebSockets, HTTPS, and routes. Don't use `express`.
- `bun:sqlite` for SQLite. Don't use `better-sqlite3`.
- `Bun.redis` for Redis. Don't use `ioredis`.
- `Bun.sql` for Postgres. Don't use `pg` or `postgres.js`.
- `WebSocket` is built-in. Don't use `ws`.
- Prefer `Bun.file` over `node:fs`'s readFile/writeFile
- Bun.$`ls` instead of execa.

## Testing

Use `bun test` to run tests.

```ts#index.test.ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";

test("hello world", () => {
  expect(1).toBe(1);
});
```

## Type checking

Use `bun check` to type check the project. It reads `tsconfig.json` and reports the same errors as `tsc`.

- `bun check src/index.ts` checks one file and what it imports
- `bun --check src/index.ts`, `bun test --check` and `bun build --check` type check first, and do nothing else if there is an error

## Frontend

Use HTML imports with `Bun.serve()`. Don't use `vite`. HTML imports fully support React, CSS, Tailwind.

Server:

```ts#index.ts
import index from "./index.html"

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": index,
    "/api/users/:id": {
      GET: (req) => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: req.params.id }));
      },
    },
  },
  // optional websocket support
  websocket: {
    open: (ws) => {
      ws.send("Hello, world!");
    },
    message: (ws, message) => {
      ws.send(message);
    },
    close: (ws) => {
      // handle close
    }
  },
  development: {
    hmr: true,
    console: true,
  }
})
```

HTML files can import .tsx, .jsx or .js files directly and Bun's bundler will transpile & bundle automatically. `<link>` tags can point to stylesheets and Bun's CSS bundler will bundle.

```html#index.html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
    <script type="module" src="./frontend.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

With the following `frontend.tsx`:

```tsx#frontend.tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

// import .css files directly and it works
import './index.css';

const root = createRoot(document.body);

export default function Frontend() {
  return <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
}

root.render(<Frontend />);
```

Then, run index.ts

```sh
bun --hot ./index.ts
```

For more information, read the Bun API docs in `docs/**.mdx`.

## What I found

**1. Built-in copy of the three rule files: feasible.** Bun can run a small function at build time (a "macro") that reads `rules/*.json` and writes their contents into `dist/index.js`. The bun-types shipped here support this in TypeScript, so the declaration-build problem from my earlier message goes away. I still need to confirm by running it that the macro also works in `bun test` and `bun src/cli.ts`.

**2. opencode only checks `engines.opencode` for npm entries.** In 1.19.3 the check sits behind `if (source === "npm")`. A `file://` copy runs whatever the opencode version, so "skipped because of its version" can only happen to an npm entry. The README finding "`engines.opencode` is enforced" is half wrong, and I'll correct it.

## What changes with the built-in copy

When a rule file on disk is broken:

| | Today | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agents | ask before every command | the full rules from the last build |
| Write guard | on, except when `commands.json` is broken | always on |
| Tools, `/guard-review` | not registered | registered |
| Log and toast | `error` with `where: load` | `error` with `where: "rules"` naming the file, plus `init.builtin: ["allow.json"]`; toast: "…cannot be read, using the rules built into the plugin; fix the file or rebuild" |

- A file on disk that reads fine always wins, so editing rules in a checkout still needs no rebuild.
- The fallback is in `rules.ts`, so `check` and `rules` use it too and print a warning on stderr.
- Fail closed remains for a failing config hook, and as a backstop if a build ever lacks the built-in copy.
- `mise.toml`: the `build` task gets `rules/*.json` in its `sources`. Otherwise `mise run build` would skip the rebuild after a rule change and keep an old built-in copy.

## The version check, adjusted

doctor runs `opencode --version` and compares it with each of our entries' `engines.opencode`:
- **npm entry outside its range:** "not loaded: skipped by opencode, requires >=1.18.29 <2, this is 2.0.1". doctor can't read the manifest opencode installed, so it uses its own package's range and says so.
- **`file://` entry outside its range:** a warning that opencode doesn't check this for path plugins and that the plugin may not work, for example on 2.x, where v1 plugins don't run.
- **Range forms other than `>=`, `<` and `||`:** reported as "not checked".

The npm import check stays in TODO, linked to "Publish to npm".

232:   guardLog: GuardLog,

236:   const { client, worktree } = pluginInput
237:   const readOnly = new Set<string>()
238:   const sessions = createSessions(client)
239:   const asks = new Map<string, AskRecord>()
240:   // Registered once the setup above succeeded: a copy that fails to start never takes charge.

244:   })
245:   const guard = writeGuard(analyzer, sessions, readOnly, guardLog, worktree)
246: 
247:   const applyPolicy = (config: MutableConfig) => {
248:     for (const warning of options.warnings) guardLog.write({ type: "error", where: "options", error: warning })
249:     const { store, include, exclude } = agentLists(options, (error) =>
250:       guardLog.write({ type: "error", where: "store", error: String(error.cause ?? error) }),
251:     )
252:     const herdr = loadHerdrRules(options, (error) =>
253:       guardLog.write({ type: "error", where: "herdr config", error: String(error.cause ?? error) }),
254:     )
255:     const effective = effectiveRules({ commands: rules.commands, store, options, herdr })
256:     for (const problem of effective.problems) guardLog.write({ type: "error", ...problem })
257:     const names = injectRules(config, { rules, learned: effective.patterns, include, exclude })
258:     readOnly.clear()
259:     for (const name of names) readOnly.add(name)
260:     if (options.command) registerReviewCommand(config, options.command)
261:     guardLog.write({
262:       type: "init",
263:       project: worktree,
264:       roAgents: [...names],

269:       failed: failedCopies(pluginInput).map(({ module, error }) => ({ module, error })),
270:     })
271:   }
272: 
273:   // Every hook of a copy that is not in charge returns at once (another copy of the plugin was loaded after it).

276:       if (!copy.active()) return

Git shows the file as a delete plus an add rather than a rename, since the content changed a lot, which is fine. Next is the doctor command: if the startup reports a built-in copy of the rules file that can't be read, I'll add a warning saying the built-in copy is what applies and the file needs fixing or a rebuild, and I'll check how existing rule errors are already labelled in the report.

I'm adding a warning for the built-in rules copy, and the version check next: I'll run `opencode --version`, pull the version number from the output, and write a `satisfies` helper that handles the range forms I need.

I'm going over the partial-version rules for the range check: `<` and `>=` can take a partial version and get padded with zeros, but `>`, `<=`, `=`, and bare versions will only be checked when they're full versions. Any version with a prerelease tag, or an invalid one, gets skipped, and the check doesn't run at all when the major version is 0.

I'm working out how to handle the version range for the npm and file entries. For npm, I'd read the range from this package's own `engines.opencode`, and if the version doesn't match, opencode skips the plugin, so I'd mark that entry with an error. For file entries I'd read it from the directory's package.json, and a mismatch becomes a warning instead.

I'm adding the version-range check for the file and npm entries: a mismatch with the file's `engines.opencode` becomes a warning, and an npm entry out of range gets marked as skipped. If the range can't be parsed, I'll note it as not checked, and if `opencode --version` fails I'll warn that the version couldn't be determined.

I'm writing unit tests for the version check now, starting with one where a path plugin outside its declared range still loads but gets a warning.

I'm adding tests for the version-range helper, covering cases that should pass or fail and cases that should come back as not checked, and I'll add a test that a builtin rules copy that can't be read produces a warning.

I'm adding tests for the doctor command now: a `checkout()` helper that can take engines in its manifest, an integration case where a copy declaring `engines.opencode` ">=99" still loads with a warning, and an assertion that the corrupt-rules test sees the "built into" warning. I'll write the unit tests first.

67: anything: run `opencode-readonly-guard doctor` in the project to check.
68: 
69: ## Using it
70: 
71: **`/guard-review`** (registered by the plugin, runs in `build`) summarizes the log: blocked commands, the most-prompted
72: commands and allowlist candidates. For each candidate you pick the exact rule to keep (the exact command, the same
73: command limited to its directory, or opencode's general pattern, whichever the safety check accepts) or dismiss it.
74: opencode then asks you to confirm that exact pattern before it is written to `readonly-guard.json`. New rules apply
75: after a restart. In read-only agents the review tools are hidden, so an agent cannot extend its own allowlist.
76: 
77: **Command-line tool** (`opencode-readonly-guard`, also available as `npx opencode-readonly-guard`):
78: 
79: ```text
80: check [--json] [--no-store] <command>   what a read-only agent gets: allow | ask | block (exit status 0 | 1 | 2)
81: vet <pattern>                           may this pattern be added to the allowlist?
82: rules [--json]                          print the shared allowlist and the always-ask flags
83: review [--limit N]                      print the log summary
84: install [-g] [--force]                  opencode plugin opencode-readonly-guard
85: doctor [--json]                         is the guard active here? (exit status 0 | 1)
86: ```
87: 
88: ```console
89: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'git log --oneline | head'
90: allow
91: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'ls | cat > notes.txt'
92: block  write redirection "> notes.txt"
93: $ opencode-readonly-guard check 'uptime'
94: ask    needs approval: uptime
95: ```
96: 
97: `doctor` starts opencode in the current directory without a model (`opencode debug config`, the plugin's log for that
98: run goes to a temporary directory) and reports: this plugin's entries in the config and which one is in charge, why a
99: `file://` copy cannot be imported (`dist/index.js is missing: a checkout that was not built, run mise run build in
100: …`), which agents carry the guard's rules and how many, the errors of that start, and the last start logged for the
101: project. It exits with 1 when the guard is not active, including when it failed closed; `--json` prints the report.
102:

203: `READONLY_GUARD_STORE` and `READONLY_GUARD_DATA` override the default paths (an explicit option wins). The store file
204: is plain JSON and safe to keep in your dotfiles; the event log contains the commands your agents ran, so keep it local.

206: copies of the plugin loaded or `failed` (see [Install](#install)); a copy that fails closed logs an `error` event
207: instead (`where`: `load` or `config`, `writeGuard`: whether the write guard is still on).
208: 
209: ## What it does not do
210: 
211: This is an accident preventer and a policy engine, not a sandbox.
212: 
213: - Only the `bash`/`shell` tool is covered. MCP tools, `webfetch` and others follow opencode's normal permissions.
214: - Interpreters can write (`python -c`, `node -e`, `awk`, `sqlite3 .shell`). They are not on the allowlist, so they
215:   prompt, but the guard does not read their code, and a broad "always" answer would let them through.
216: - Parsing is a hand-written approximation of POSIX shell; anything it cannot parse is blocked rather than guessed.
217: - Linux and macOS shells only. PowerShell is not parsed.
218: - "Always" answers made in opencode itself stay in effect for all agents until restart, see the findings below. The
219:   plugin warns, logs them and keeps the write guard on top, but it cannot revoke them.
220: 
221: ## Findings about opencode 1.19.3
222: 
223: What building this taught us. Each point was checked against the binary or by a live run, and several are worth an
224: upstream issue (they are in [TODO.md](TODO.md)).
225: 
226: **Permissions**
227: 
228: - Plan mode is a prompt. The `plan` agent only denies the `edit` tool (except plan files); its `bash` is `* allow`
229:   and so is `explore`'s. The "READ-ONLY phase" text is a reminder injected into the conversation.
230: - Rules are evaluated in order and the last match wins; `*` matches anything and a trailing ` *` also matches the bare
231:   command.
232: - Bash commands are split with tree-sitter and each simple command is matched on its own text. That text includes a
233:   redirection only when the command's direct parent is the redirection, so `cat a > b` is matched as written, while
234:   the redirections of later pipeline stages (`a | b > f`), `{ …; } > f` and `( … ) > f` are invisible to patterns.
235:   Glob rules therefore cannot stop those writes; a parser in `tool.execute.before` can.
236: - Commands inside `$(…)`, backticks and `<(…)` are checked as separate commands.
237: 
238: **"Always" answers**
239: 
240: - The saved pattern is the command prefix plus `*`, using a built-in table of how many words matter (`git log *`,
241:   `npm view *`) and falling back to the first word. Unknown programs become `prog *`: answering "always" to
242:   `tee /dev/null` allowed `tee *`, and for anything rewritten by the rtk plugin it is `rtk *`.
243: - It is kept in memory for the whole opencode process, is checked after every agent's rules (so it beats `ask` and
244:   `deny`), applies to all agents and sessions, and is lost on restart. The `permission` table in the database stays
245:   empty.
246: 
247: **Plugin API**
248: 
249: - `tool.execute.before` runs before the permission check; throwing from it aborts the tool call and the message reaches
250:   the model. This is what makes the write guard possible.
251: - The `permission.ask` hook is declared in the types and docs but is never called. A plugin cannot answer prompts
252:   itself, so learning has to go through a review step.
253: - The `config` hook may edit `agent.<name>.permission`; the rules end up after the built-in ones in the resolved
254:   agent (`opencode debug agent <name>` shows them). A permission set globally is appended after every agent's rules.
255: - `chat.params` reports the agent of each model call, including subagents. The utility agents `title`, `summary` and
256:   `compaction` share the session, so they must be ignored when tracking which agent a session belongs to. The v1 SDK
257:   types do not expose `agent` on sessions, but the runtime does (used as a fallback).
258: - Permission events are `permission.asked` / `permission.replied` at runtime, although the v1 SDK types still say
259:   `permission.updated`.
260: - Plugin tools can call `context.ask()` to raise a permission prompt. Agents start from `* allow`, so the plugin adds a
261:   global `readonly_guard_allow: ask` rule (evaluated after every agent's rules) to force the confirmation prompt.
262: 
263: **Plugin packaging (v1)**
264: 
265: - opencode treats every export of a plugin module as a plugin and calls it. Export only the default definition.
266: - A package is loaded from `exports["./server"]`, else `main`. A default export `{ id, server }` is supported since
267:   1.18.29. `engines.opencode` is enforced. Peer dependencies such as `@opencode-ai/plugin` are installed for you.
268: - That install only happens for npm packages. A plugin loaded from a path (`file://…`) resolves its imports from that
269:   path, and if one fails (no `node_modules` there) opencode drops the plugin without a log line, even at `DEBUG`, while
270:   `opencode debug config` still lists it. This is why `dist/` is a bundle that only imports Node built-ins. The same
271:   goes for a checkout without `dist/` and for a `file://` path that does not exist: `opencode debug config` exits 0
272:   with nothing on stderr, and opencode starts as if nothing were wrong. A plugin that fails to import cannot report
273:   anything itself; only an outside check can (`opencode-readonly-guard doctor`).
274: - A plugin whose `server()` throws is dropped too, with one `failed to load plugin` line in opencode's log; an error
275:   in a `config` hook is logged (`plugin config hook failed`) and opencode goes on. Either way the agents keep whatever
276:   the config holds at that point, which is why this plugin catches its own errors and fails closed.
277: - A toast sent while opencode starts (from `server()` or a `config` hook, without awaiting it: the request waits for
278:   the instance being started) reaches clients listening to the global event stream, which the TUI does.
279: - Plugin entries are merged only when they name the same `file://` URL or npm package (the last one is kept). Two

72:   (`git branch -a --edit-desc`, `-rd`), `sort --out=FILE`, and `uniq - OUT` / `uniq IN 5`. It blocked
73:   `git tag -n1 NAME`, which lists.
74: - The write guard blocked listings: bare `mount`, `systemctl show-environment|get-default`, and systemctl read verbs
75:   after an option that takes a value (`systemctl -t service list-units`). It missed journalctl's maintenance options
76:   when abbreviated (`--rot`, `--vac=1d`).
77: - `/guard-review` proposed already allowed stages of compound commands: every candidate was offered the general

79:   still ask about count now, each with its own general pattern.

81:   restored without `node_modules`, a copy of `dist/` and `rules/`), it failed to import and opencode dropped it without a

83:   built-ins (zod is included, its licence is in `dist/zod.LICENSE`).
84: - A plugin configured twice with different specs (a global and a project entry, two checkouts) ran twice: both copies
85:   injected rules, registered the review tools and logged every event. Only the copy loaded last runs now, which is the
86:   project's entry, and its options replace the global ones (they are not merged). The `init` event names the copy in

59:   `<program> <subcommand> --help` commands). `inject.ts`: finds the read-only agents and writes their rules into

62: - `sources.ts`: presets (`herdr-ui`) and the merge of options, store and herdr's file. `options.ts`: plugin options
63:   and default paths.
64: - `store.ts`: learned rules (`readonly-guard.json`). `log.ts`: the event log (`events.jsonl`, rotated).
65: - `review.ts`, `tools.ts`, `command.ts`: the log summary, the `readonly_guard_review` and `readonly_guard_update`

67: - `commands.ts`, `cli.ts`: the command-line tool. `doctor.ts`: its `doctor` subcommand (runs `opencode debug config`

70: `rules/`: `allow.json`, `ask.json`, `commands.json`, `cases.json` and their JSON Schemas in `schema/` (CONTRIBUTING.md
71: describes each file). They ship in the npm package and are read at runtime.
72: 
73: `test/`
74: 
75: - `unit/`: mostly one file per module. `cases.test.ts` runs every case in `rules/cases.json`; `rules.test.ts` checks
76:   the rule files against each other.
77: - `integration/`: the real opencode without a model (`opencode debug config|agent` in a sandbox project), two copies
78:   of the plugin in one opencode, copies with corrupt rule files, `doctor`, and the packed tarball. Broken copies are
79:   `file://` copies of the build (`copyPlugin()`); never put an unpublished npm name in a config, opencode would
80:   install whatever the registry serves under it.
81: - `e2e/`: a real model drives a read-only harness agent; opt-in (`OPENCODE_E2E=1`, set by the mise task).
82: - `helpers.ts`: `sandbox()`, a throwaway project with its own XDG directories, store and log (and, with

I pushed four new commits to PR #12: the write guard now survives a broken `commands.json`, and doctor now checks the opencode version. I also updated the PR description. Locally, `mise run check` passes (933 tests) and `mise run test:integration` passes (30 tests, 0 failures). CI hasn't run on these commits yet; it was green on the earlier ones.

**1. A copy of the rule files built into the plugin** (you chose all three files)
- `mise run build` now writes a copy of `allow.json`, `ask.json` and `commands.json` into `dist/`. It adds about 50 KB to each bundle.
- If a rule file on disk is corrupt, missing or the wrong shape, that copy replaces it. Read-only agents keep the full rules and the write guard, and `/guard-review` stays registered. Tested with a broken `allow.json`, with broken `commands.json` and `ask.json`, and with no `rules/` folder at all.
- You are told in three places: an `error` line naming the file, the `init` line listing it under `builtin`, and a warning toast. The command-line tool also warns on stderr.
- A file that reads fine is always used, so editing rules in a checkout still needs no rebuild.
- `mise run build` now also rebuilds when a rule file changes, so the copy doesn't go stale.
- **One thing to know:** if a rule file breaks, the copy from the last build applies, which can be older than your working tree. The toast and doctor say so.
- "Everything asks" (fail closed) still exists, but only for an error inside our own code at startup, or a build without the copy.

**2. The two gaps**
- **opencode version check: fixed.** opencode only checks `engines.opencode` for npm packages; a `file://` copy loads whatever its range says. A test confirms it with a copy that requires opencode `>=99`: it loads and is in charge. The README said the check was always enforced; I corrected it. doctor now runs `opencode --version`:
  - an npm entry outside its range is reported as "skipped by opencode: requires …, this is …";
  - a `file://` entry outside its range gets a warning that it may not work.
- **Checking that npm entries can be imported: left in TODO.** It can't be tested until the package is published, and a stand-in npm name in a config is ruled out. The item is now linked to "Publish to npm".

**doctor's exit status:** when a rule file was replaced by the built-in copy, doctor exits 0 with a warning, since the guard is active. You didn't object to that.

globalPlugin?: string } = {}): Sandbox {\n  const box = sandbox({ plugin: \".\", globalPlugin })\n  cleanup.push(() => box.cleanup())\n  copyPlugin(box.project)\n  mkdirSync(join(box.project, \"src\"))\n  if (!built) rmSync(join(box.project, \"dist\"), { recursive: true })\n  return box\n}\n\n/** A checkout elsewhere (the main one), built, and its `file://` spec. */\nfunction mainCheckout(): { dir: string; spec: string } {\n  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), \"rg-main-\"))\n  cleanup.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))\n  return { dir, spec: copyPlugin(dir) }\n}\n\nconst moduleIn = (dir: string) => pathToFileURL(join(dir, \"dist\", \"index.js\")).href\nconst inits = (events: LogEvent[]) => events.filter((event) => event.type === \"init\")\n\n/** An agent's bash rules, and the events of the one opencode process that resolved them. */\nfunction resolve(box: Sandbox, agent = \"plan\"): { rules: RuleEntry[]; bash: string[]; events: LogEvent[] } {\n  const before = box.events().length\n  const rules = agentRules(box, agent)\n    .filter((rule) => rule.permission === \"bash\")\n    .map((rule): RuleEntry => [rule.pattern, rule.action as Action])\n  return { rules, bash: rules.map(([pattern, action]) => `${pattern}=${action}`), events: box.events().slice(before) }\n}\n\n/** The rules the plugin injects (from its `\"*\": ask` on), in a checkout configured with `\".\"` alone. */\nlet baseline: string[] | undefined\nfunction pluginRules(bash: string[]): string[] {\n  return bash.slice(bash.lastIndexOf(\"*=ask\"))\n}\nfunction baselineRules(): string[] {\n  baseline ??= pluginRules(resolve(checkout()).bash)\n  return baseline\n}\n\n// This repository's opencode.json loads its own build: \"plugin\": [\".\"], which opencode resolves to file://<checkout>.\ndescribe.skipIf(!hasOpencode)(\"a checkout that loads its own build\", () => {\n  test(\"(a) without dist/ it is skipped without a word: opencode starts, a session opens, doctor says why\", async () => {\n    const box = checkout({ built: false })\n    const config = box.opencode([\"debug\", \"config\"])\n    expect(config.status).toBe(0)\n    expect(config.stderr).toBe(\"\")\n    const origins = (JSON.parse(config.stdout) as { plugin_origins: { spec: unknown }[] }).plugin_origins\n    expect(origins.map((origin) => origin.spec)).toEqual([pathToFileURL(box.project).href])\n\n    const session = await withServer(box, async (url) => {\n      const response = await fetch(`${url}/session`, {\n        method: \"POST\",\n        headers: { \"x-opencode-directory\": box.project, \"content-type\": \"application/json\" },\n        body: \"{}\",\n      })\n      return { status: response.status, body: (await response.json()) as { id?: unknown; directory?: unknown } }\n    })\n    expect(session.status).toBe(200)\n    expect(typeof session.body.id).toBe(\"string\")\n    expect(session.body.directory).toBe(box.project)\n    expect(box.events()).toEqual([])\n\n    const doctor = runDoctor(box)\n    expect(doctor.status).toBe(1)\n    expect(doctor.stdout).toContain(\n      `dist/index.js is missing: a checkout that was not built, run \\`mise run build\\` in ${box.project}`,\n    )\n    expect(doctor.stdout).toContain(\"Guard NOT active: no copy of the plugin started\")\n  })\n\n  test(\"(b) with a global entry to the same checkout: one copy in charge, one init, the rules once\", () => {\n    const expected = baselineRules()\n    // opencode merges the same spec; with a trailing slash it keeps both entries, which import the same module\n    for (const [suffix, entries] of [\n      [\"\", 1],\n      [\"/\", 2],\n    ] as const) {\n      const box = checkout()\n      box.writeGlobalPlugin(`${pathToFileURL(box.project).href}${suffix}`)\n      const { bash, events } = resolve(box)\n      expect(inits(events)).toMatchObject([{ module: moduleIn(box.project) }])\n      expect(inits(events)[0].copies).toEqual(Array(entries).fill(moduleIn(box.project)))\n      expect(bash).toEqual(expected)\n      expect(new Set(bash).size).toBe(bash.length)\n    }\n  })\n\n  test(\"(c) a worktree's own build is in charge over a global entry to the main checkout; unbuilt, the main one guards it\", () => {\n    const main = mainCheckout()\n    const built = checkout({ globalPlugin: main.spec })\n    const worktree = resolve(built)\n    expect(inits(worktree.events)).toMatchObject([\n      { module: moduleIn(built.project), copies: [moduleIn(main.dir), moduleIn(built.project)] },\n    ])\n    expect(worktree.bash).toEqual(baselineRules())\n\n    const unbuilt = checkout({ built: false, globalPlugin: main.spec })\n    const fallback = resolve(unbuilt)\n    expect(inits(fallback.events)).toMatchObject([{ module: moduleIn(main.dir), copies: [moduleIn(main.dir)] }])\n    expect(fallback.bash).toEqual(baselineRules())\n    const doctor = runDoctor(unbuilt)\n    expect(doctor.status).toBe(0)\n    expect(doctor.stdout).toContain(`${pathToFileURL(unbuilt.project).href} was not loaded: dist/index.js is missing`)\n  })\n\n  test(\"(d) this repository's opencode.json loads the checkout's build once; read-only agents get the shared rules\", () => {\n    const box = checkout()\n    box.write(\"opencode.json\", readFileSync(join(repoRoot, \"opencode.json\"), \"utf8\"))\n    const plan = resolve(box)\n    expect(inits(plan.events)).toMatchObject([{ module: moduleIn(box.project), copies: [moduleIn(box.project)] }])\n    // the plugin's rules, once, after the repository's own\n    expect(pluginRules(plan.bash)).toEqual(baselineRules())\n    expect(evaluate(\"ls -la\", plan.rules)).toBe(\"allow\")\n    expect(evaluate(\"git status\", plan.rules)).toBe(\"allow\")\n    expect(evaluate(\"rm -rf dist\", plan.rules)).toBe(\"ask\")\n    // the repository's allowances come before the plugin's \"*\": ask, so in read-only agents only the shared\n    // allowlist runs without a prompt; build keeps them\n    expect(evaluate(\"mise run check\", plan.rules)).toBe(\"ask\")\n    expect(evaluate(\"gh pr view 12\", plan.rules)).toBe(\"ask\")\n    const build = resolve(box, \"build\")\n    expect(evaluate(\"mise run check\", build.rules)).toBe(\"allow\")\n    expect(evaluate(\"gh pr view 12\", build.rules)).toBe(\"allow\")\n  })\n})\n"

## Loading

- [x] Guarantee the plugin runs once per opencode instance. The copies of the plugin find each other through a
      versioned `globalThis` key (`src/copies.ts`), and the copy loaded last (the project's entry) is in charge with
      its own options; the others skip every hook and register no tools. Covered by `test/integration/copies.test.ts`.
  - [ ] It relies on opencode running every `server()` before any `config` hook and reading `hooks.tool` after
        them (1.19.3). If a release interleaves them, the first copy injects too, and the copy in charge then takes
        the injected rules for the agent's own. The integration test catches it on an opencode bump; a fix would
        keep each agent's pre-injection permission in the shared registry.
  - [ ] Copies built before the guard do not take part and still run next to a new one.
- [x] Load without the runtime dependency: when loaded from a path, the plugin must not need `@opencode-ai/plugin` in
      a `node_modules`. The build bundles it (and zod) into `dist/index.js`; opencode's other way, plain JSON Schema
      tool arguments, is a legacy path that makes every argument required and validates none.
- [x] Detect and report a plugin that fails to load instead of being dropped silently. A rule file that cannot be read
      is replaced by the copy built into the plugin (`src/embed.ts`), with an `error` event and a toast; a copy that
      fails in its config hook fails closed (read-only agents ask before every command, the write guard stays on); a
      copy that started takes over and lists a failed one in `init.failed`. A copy that cannot be imported runs no
      code: `opencode-readonly-guard doctor` finds it, and names an npm entry outside its `engines.opencode` range
      (covered by `test/integration/builtin.test.ts` and `doctor.test.ts`).
  - [ ] npm entries are not import-checked (opencode installs them in its own cache); doctor only reports whether
        such a copy started. Do it once the package is published (see "Release"), and test it against the real
        package: an unpublished name must never appear in a config.
- [x] Add an integration test that loads the built plugin from a directory without `node_modules` (the packed
      tarball, unpacked as is).

## Repository

- [x] opencode project config for contributors: an `AGENTS.md` with the commands and conventions, `opencode.json`
      with a `permission` setup that allows the check tasks and read-only `git`/`gh`, and the project commands
      `/check` and `/add-rule` in `.opencode/commands/`.
  - [ ] Load the repository's own plugin from `dist/` for dogfooding. A global copy no longer runs next to it (the
        project's copy wins); what remains is proving that a checkout without a build fails soft, see "Loading".
- [x] Automated dependency updates: Renovate (`renovate.json`; Dependabot handles neither `mise.toml` nor bun) for
      npm and `bun.lock`, `mise.toml` (opencode included), `hk.pkl` and the GitHub Actions (pinned to SHAs), with
      grouped minor/patch updates and `build(deps):` / `ci(deps):` commits.
  - [ ] Enable the Renovate GitHub app on the repository, then merge its first "opencode" pull request (the pinned
        opencode bump) once `mise run test:integration` passes against it.

## Testing
## Development

Everything is managed with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev); Git hooks with [hk](https://hk.jdx.dev).

```sh
mise install                # bun, node, hk, actionlint, shellcheck and the pinned opencode
mise run setup              # bun install + git hooks (prettier, oxlint, tsc, conventional commits)
mise run check              # lint, formatting, types, unit tests (what CI runs)
mise run test:integration   # builds, then drives the real opencode without a model, and a packed tarball
mise run test:e2e           # opt-in, real model: E2E_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
mise tasks                  # all tasks
```

Code style follows opencode: TypeScript (strict, NodeNext), no semicolons, 120 columns, oxlint, prettier. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for adding rules and test cases.

## Assistant (Build · Claude Opus 5.5 · 9.9s)

PR B is open as #14 (not merged): the repository's `opencode.json` now has `"plugin": ["."]`. Locally, `mise run check` passes (1114 tests) and `mise run test:integration` passes (34 tests, 0 failures); CI hadn't reported yet when I wrote this.

The new `test/integration/dogfood.test.ts` checks four cases:
- **(a) A checkout without `dist/`:** opencode silently skips the entry, still starts and opens a session. doctor exits 1 and says to run `mise run build` in that checkout.
- **(b) A global entry pointing at the same checkout:** one copy loads, with one `init` line, and the rules are injected once. That holds with the same spec, and with a trailing slash, where opencode keeps both entries but they load the same file.
- **(c) A worktree with its own build, plus a global entry to the main checkout:** the worktree's copy is in charge. Without a build, the main checkout's copy guards the worktree, and doctor exits 0 with a warning that the worktree's entry wasn't loaded.
- **(d) The repository's real `opencode.json`:** one copy loads and the rules appear once. This test was written first and failed before the config change; (a) to (c) describe opencode's current behaviour and passed from the start.

**Doubled rules:** none in any case. On the live machine, doctor run from this worktree shows the global entry passive, this worktree's build in charge, and 1915 rules each for plan and explore, the same as the global install alone. doctor only read your real config; the plugin's log and store went to scratch paths. opencode may still have written its own files under `~/.local/share/opencode` during that run, as it does on any start.

**One behaviour change to know about:** in this repository, plan and explore now ask before `mise run check`, `bun src/cli.ts` and `gh` commands. The plugin's "ask for everything" rule comes after the repository's allowances and wins in read-only agents. Only the shared allowlist runs without a prompt there; build is unaffected. This is in AGENTS.md.

**Docs:**
- AGENTS.md: the new `opencode.json` entry; the note that the project entry's options replace a global entry's (for other contributors, since yours has none); and a hazard paragraph. A worktree's build guards that worktree's sessions, and `mise run build` there only reaches sessions started in it afterwards. Without a build, the global copy guards it.
- README: a development note and a from-source hint.
